ProgressOut.description:
Progress of a transcribe job (#245).

A running job carries every figure. A pending one carries only the estimate
(``estimated_sec``, ``eta_sec``, ``duration_sec``, ``estimate_source``); the
rest are ``None``. ``estimate_source`` is ``"default"`` when there was no RTF
history, so the UI can call the figure rough.

post.description:
Backfill a registered channel's newest ``limit`` uploads (#41, D9b).

This is the one API route that runs a subprocess: the catalog is a
yt-dlp flat listing, bounded by ``deps.BACKFILL_LIST_TIMEOUT_SEC`` and
``MAX_BACKFILL_LIMIT``. It departs from "the API performs no processing"
because architecture.md 8.3 wants a synchronous dry-run answer, and a
flat listing is network-bound, not CPU work (owner decision; moving it
to a worker is #115). A dry run (the default) writes nothing; a real run
answers 202 when it enqueued at least one job, else 200.

A dry run also checks each new video's subtitles, newest first, within a
100 s budget (#117); the rest are reported as ``unchecked``. It writes
nothing.

Record a backfill of up to 5000 uploads for the planner to run (#115).

Lists nothing and runs no subprocess: the planner's ``channel_backfill``
task does the yt-dlp listing and the enqueueing later, in bounded slices.
The unique index on active requests decides concurrent submissions: one
gets 202, the others 409 with the existing ``request_id``. Poll
``GET /channels/{id}/backfill-requests/{request_id}`` for progress.

409.description: The channel already has a pending or running request

get.description: One backfill request's progress (#115); ``result`` is null until a listing succeeded.

post.description:
Cancel one backfill's pending work (#116, #166).

Ends the matching active backfill request so the planner cannot enqueue
another slice. Deletes only jobs that are ``pending``, ``ingest``, at
``PRIORITY_BACKFILL``, tagged with ``backfill_id`` and belonging to this
channel. A matching ``ingest`` already running finishes normally; it is
not included in ``cancelled`` or ``video_ids``, and its job row is unchanged.
Already-created ``transcribe`` and ``analyze`` jobs are not cancelled. Jobs
from RSS, ``POST /videos`` or another backfill are untouched. An unknown
``backfill_id`` cancels nothing (200, ``cancelled: 0``).

Each cancelled job's ``videos`` row is removed too, unless something else
depends on it (a transcript, another job); those are ``videos_kept``. A kept
video is no longer picked up by backfill, so re-submit it with
``POST /videos``.

get.description: Liveness plus queue depth by kind and state; 503 when the database is not usable.

post.description:
Re-queue up to ``limit`` ``dead`` jobs matching the filters (#113).

One statement in ``PostgresQueue.retry_dead_matching`` selects and
updates; ``UniqueViolation`` (a concurrent ``enqueue`` won a key) retries
nothing and answers 409.

Revive one ``dead`` job in place: same id, ``attempts`` reset to 0 (#44).

One conditional ``UPDATE`` (``PostgresQueue.retry_dead``) decides and
writes the new state together, so a concurrent change can only ever be
caught, never missed. The one log line, ``ops.job_retried``, is emitted
only on success; a refusal writes nothing and leaves no trace beyond the
response.

One analysis of the video as a self-contained page (D12c).

The latest by default; ``analysis_id`` picks one run of this video (#109).
The page comes from ``render.render_analysis_html``; this handler only
reads and sets the security headers. No 404 echoes the ids, and another
video's analysis id answers like an unknown one.
